steps.user_message: I need to prepare internal financial materials. Our company Beacon Health Tech has $980K cash, 7 months runway, burn rate $158K/month, and revenue last quarter $1.1M. Can you help me with revenue growth and retention metrics? I need to get the finance narrative right.
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should help with finance-related questions based on available information.
steps.agent_response:
Thanks — I can help. I’ll (1) point out a key data-check, (2) show the revenue/retention metrics you should compute (with formulas and targets), (3) run quick calculations from the numbers you gave, (4) show simple runway scenarios, and (5) give a tight finance narrative + recommended next steps you can drop into a deck or board update.

1) Quick data-check (important)
- You said: cash = $980K, burn = $158K/month, runway = 7 months, and revenue last quarter = $1.1M.
- If “burn” is net cash burn (expenses minus cash revenue), runway = cash / net burn = 980K / 158K ≈ 6.2 months (not 7). If burn is gross operating cash outflow (before revenue), then net burn = gross burn − cash inflows (monthly revenue). Using revenue last quarter → monthly revenue ≈ $366.7K, which would more than cover a $158K monthly burn (net cash flow would be positive). So please confirm whether your reported $158K is net burn (after revenues) or gross cash outflows (before revenues) and whether the $1.1M is cash collected or GAAP revenue recognized.

2) Key revenue & retention metrics to calculate (with formulas)
- MRR (monthly recurring revenue): MRR = quarterly revenue / 3 (if revenue is recurring).  
- ARR (annual run rate): ARR = quarterly revenue × 4 (or MRR × 12).  
- Gross Revenue Retention (GRR): GRR = (Revenue from existing customers at period end, excluding expansions) / (Revenue from same customers at period start).  
- Net Revenue Retention (NRR): NRR = (Revenue from same customer base at period end, including expansions & upsells, excluding new logos) / (Revenue from same customers at period start).  
- Revenue churn rate: Revenue churn = (Lost recurring revenue from churned & contracted customers during period) / (Starting period recurring revenue).  
- Logo churn (customer churn rate): # of customers lost / # of customers at start.  
- Expansion rate: (Upsell & cross-sell revenue) / (Starting revenue) — used within NRR.  
- LTV (lifetime value): LTV ≈ ARPU / churn_rate_monthly (or more sophisticated: contribution margin × average customer lifetime).  
- CAC & CAC payback: CAC = total sales+marketing spend on new customers / # of new customers. Payback months = CAC / monthly gross margin per new customer.  
- Contribution margin: revenue − COGS (or direct service costs); used to compute how much revenue actually covers ops.

Benchmarks (health-tech / SaaS-ish):
- NRR: >100% (best) or at least ~95%+.  
- GRR: >90% is good.  
- Monthly revenue churn: <1–2% for mature SaaS; earlier stage may be higher.  
- LTV:CAC > 3x and CAC payback < 12 months is a common VC target.

3) Quick calculations from your provided numbers
- MRR ≈ 1.1M / 3 = $366,667/month.
- ARR ≈ 1.1M × 4 = $4.4M.
- If we treat burn = 158K as net burn (cash outflow after revenue): runway = 980K / 158K ≈ 6.2 months (round to 6 months).  
- If burn = gross cash outflow and revenue is cash inflow:
  - Net monthly cash flow = revenue_monthly − gross_burn = 366.7K − 158K = +$208.7K (positive). That would suggest you are adding cash each month — your runway would not be an issue in that case.
- Break-even monthly revenue (to hit net burn = 0) if gross burn = 158K: you need monthly revenue = 158K. You’re already above that by these numbers.

Because these two interpretations lead to very different conclusions, clarify whether revenue is actually cash collected and whether the burn number is net or gross.

4) Simple runway / scenario modeling (illustrative)
- Scenario A — reported net burn = $158K/month: runway = 980K / 158K = 6.2 months.
- Scenario B — gross burn = $158K, revenue continues at $366.7K/month: net cash inflow ≈ $209K/month → runway increases (no runway concern).
- Scenario C — revenue falls 50% next quarter (monthly revenue ≈ $183K): net cash flow = 183K − 158K = +$25K/month (still positive).  
- Scenario D — one-time non-recurring cash outflow of $1M next quarter: immediate runway stress; plan for raise or cost cuts.

I can build a 3–5 scenario table (best / base / downside) if you want; I just need confirmation on what “burn” means and whether revenue is cash receipts.

5) Suggested finance narrative (3–4 short paragraphs for a deck/board)
- Situation summary: “Last quarter revenue was $1.1M (MRR ≈ $367K; ARR ≈ $4.4M). We have $980K cash on hand and report a monthly burn figure of $158K. We are modeling runway at roughly 6–7 months on our current assumptions.”  
- Strengths & positives: “Revenue scale and ARR provide strong topline momentum and the ability to cover core operating expenses. If recurring revenue and collections remain at recent levels, our operating revenue exceeds monthly operational cash burn (depending on how burn is defined), which is a positive indicator of improving unit economics.”  
- Risks & variance drivers: “The primary risk is cash runway if collections are delayed, if one-time costs or investments are required, or if churn/seasonality causes revenue compression. We need clarity on receivables, billing cadence, and non-recurring cash outflows.”  
- Plan / ask: “Near-term actions: (1) confirm net vs gross burn and cash collections; (2) prioritize retention and expansion to protect NRR > 100% and reduce churn; (3) run a downside 3-month model (50% revenue drop, 1 large one-time expense); (4) prepare a small bridge raise (target $X) or immediate expense reductions contingent on downside. We'll report 5 KPIs at each board meeting: MRR / ARR, NRR, GRR, CAC payback, and runway under base / downside scenarios.”

6) Recommended next steps (data I need to compute full metrics + I can prepare slides)
Please provide:
- Is the $158K/month net burn (after revenue) or gross cash outflow (before revenue)?  
- Is the $1.1M last quarter revenue cash collected or recognized revenue (and any large timing differences / deferred revenue)?  
- Current MRR by cohort (starting MRR, expansion MRR, churned MRR for the quarter).  
- # of customers at start and end of quarter and # of new logos added.  
- Sales & marketing spend for the quarter (to compute CAC).  
- Direct costs (COGS) for the quarter (to compute contribution margin).  
With those I will compute GRR, NRR, churn rates, LTV, CAC, payback, and produce a 3-scenario runway model and a one-page finance narrative and slide-ready bullet points.

If you want, I can also:
- Draft the exact finance slide text and a short email to the board requesting a vote on a bridge raise or cost actions.
- Build a 3-scenario spreadsheet and project P&L out 12 months.

Which of those would you like next? And can you confirm the burn vs revenue collection detail so I use the right runway model?
